The wave function describes measurement *possibilities*. Interaction with the system (measuring position, momentum, etc.) forces a definite outcome. No consciousness required—in fact, experiments work the same whether anyone's paying attention.

**For your students:**

You could frame it as a vocabulary problem: "The word 'observer' is terrible here. It makes people think 'person watching.' Physics just means 'any system doing a measurement.' The universe doesn't care if you're conscious."

This also inoculates them against the pseudo-scientific claims that follow from the misconception (consciousness creating reality, etc.).
